result.summary: Implemented per lib/letflow/design/req386-attachment-signed-links.md with one deliberate, in-authority implementation simplification: get_or_create_signing_key/2 in Letflow.Repository.AttachmentLinks uses a single Letflow.Secrets.resolve/2 call for the common case (secret already exists -- resolve/2 already returns both plaintext and key_id) rather than the design's two-call unpinned-then-pinned sequence, falling back to Secrets.put/2 only on a genuine :not_found; public @spec signatures, error shapes, and every security-relevant behavior (per-tenant key, key_id pinned into every token, single collapsed {:error, :expired_or_invalid} return, separate untouched content route) match the design exactly -- this is a private-helper call-count optimization, not a deviation from the approved mechanism, and does not change any externally observable behavior. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: 0 warnings, exits 0 (one unused-variable warning found and fixed during implementation -- create_signing_key/1's now-unused tenant_slug parameter removed). mix format --check-formatted: clean after `mix format` on the new file. No migration added -- verified against the live lib/letflow/secrets.ex: check_purpose_allowed(:generic, :generic) already returns :ok (line 334), confirming the design's no-migration claim rather than trusting it. Ran the existing attachment test suites to confirm no regression: mix test test/letflow/routers/req212_attachments_routes_test.exs test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs -- Result: 42 passed, 0 failures (REQ-211/212's cross-tenant/cross-instance not-found-folding tests included, unchanged). mix test test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs -- Result: 18 passed, confirming the two new endpoint_policy_key/2 clauses resolve correctly and the introspection check (__authz_routes__/0 vs endpoint_policy_key/2) is satisfied for both new routes. No INV-7 SQL-interpolation risk introduced (zero Repo.query/raw-SQL calls anywhere in the new code -- every DB touch goes through Letflow.Secrets/Letflow.Identity's existing Ecto.Query-based functions). No INV-8 bare-match risk (every AttachmentLinks function returns a tagged tuple; verify/3's with/else chain explicitly catches every external-input decode failure).
